findings.title: The filtered argument to noteUnmappedBlockReasons is unasserted: passing the WHOLE block-reason set survives all 59 cases of persist.test.ts
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant applied: `if (unmapped.length > 0) noteUnmappedBlockReasons(unmapped);` -> `... noteUnmappedBlockReasons(autoDecision.blockReasons);`. The designated case passed, and a full-file run passed 59/59. NOT equivalent: for a mixed set the helper joins and emits a DIFFERENT string, so the operator Sentry issue and the durable log line would read "...has no category mapping: rating_below_threshold, ghost_reason" — naming a mapped code as unmapped, which is exactly the operator confusion the ticket exists to remove. NOT on an unexecuted branch: the mixed case runs this line. The hole is structural — the only two cases that assert `mock.calls[0]![0]` (case 1 and the toString case) pass ALL-unmapped sets, where filtered and unfiltered are the same array; the mixed case, the one input that discriminates, asserts only `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`. write.ts:488-492 and the docs/directory.md row both state the parameter contract as "already-unmapped codes", and nothing enforces it. Fix is one line: add `expect(noteUnmappedBlockReasonsSpy.mock.calls[0]![0]).toEqual(['ghost_reason'])` to the mixed case.

findings.title: The alerting runbook still says an unmapped block reason raises nothing, and records only three warning-level emitters where HEAD has a fourth at level error
findings.reason: Three facets of the six contradict the emitted signal. (a) Line 73-77 states verbatim: "One blind spot #1079 leaves standing ... an UNMAPPED block reason (the #1080 fault class) raises nothing on this lane while the switch is off". That is FALSE at HEAD — it is precisely what this branch fixes, and the branch corrected the identical sentence in write.ts's withLedgerAttribution docblock while leaving this one standing. (b) Line 54-59 scopes the rule to issues tagged `subsystem:refusal_ledger` "at level `warning`", "Emitted by **three** callers ... all through the shared private `warnLedgerDisabled()`". HEAD adds a FOURTH emitter carrying the SAME tag at level `error` and NOT through warnLedgerDisabled. (c) The new `fault: unmapped_block_reason` tag and its grouping title have no row anywhere in the runbook, and line 312 still names `subsystem:refusal_ledger` as "the ledger's only gap detector" with no rule in either Sentry project. Operational consequence: the row teaches an operator that every `subsystem:refusal_ledger` issue is a deliberate operator state rather than a defect, and any tag-based Discord rule built from this row would silently route the new error signal under that reading — re-creating the exact confusion at the alert layer. docs/runbooks/ is NOT in allowed_edit_surface, which is why this was missed; fixing it needs surface amendment 2, itself an abort-criteria trigger (D8).

findings.title: "Promoted to lab notes." is false — lab-notes.md is unchanged on this branch and holds no #1105 or array-drop entry
findings.reason: The row's item (d) ends "Both transports now carry one joined string. Promoted to lab notes." `git diff 313a3e01..01aa07f3 --name-only` does not list `.claude/reference/lab-notes.md`; `rg "1105" .claude/reference/lab-notes.md` returns 0 and no sanitizeAnalyticsProperties / array-drop lesson exists there. The path is also outside allowed_edit_surface, so the promotion could not have happened on this branch. The branch's own deviations D6 states it in the FUTURE tense — "it is promoted to lab notes at step 8" — so two changed docs contradict each other and the arch log is the false one. "Promoted to lab notes" appears exactly once in the whole file (this row), so it is not an established shorthand for a pending action. This is the third recorded falsification of this file.

findings.reason: The comment reads "THE SIGNAL, receiving the set VERBATIM. The helper owns the membership test, so the call site hands it everything and does not pre-filter." At HEAD persist.ts:960 passes the FILTERED `unmapped`, and persist.ts:751 owns the `Object.hasOwn` test — deviations D5 records that reversal explicitly. The comment survives from the reverted design and now contradicts write.ts:488, the docs/directory.md row, the arch-review-log row and D5, all in the same diff. It is also the proximate reason F-01 is invisible: a reader of this case is told the argument is deliberately unfiltered, so the missing argument assertion looks intentional.

findings.title: "SEVEN OF THESE THIRTEEN CASES ... THE OTHER SIX" — the describe block holds twelve cases, six of them review-added
findings.reason: `describe('noteUnmappedBlockReasons')` contains 12 `it(` cases at HEAD, not 13. The plan's T1 lists 13 titles for this file, but deviations D5 MOVED one of them — [R1-4], the inherited-key case — to persist.test.ts, so 12 remain and 6 of them (not 7) came from plan review; the seventh review-added case now lives in the other file. findings.title: `_PrecedenceIsTotal` is credited with a guarantee it does not carry (unranked, not unmapped)
findings.reason: The new docblock states "SINCE #1080 A NON-EMPTY RESULT NEEDS A VALUE THAT ESCAPED THE UNION. `_PrecedenceIsTotal` makes a member with no map entry a `pnpm typecheck` failure." At src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts:658, `_PrecedenceIsTotal = AssertNever<UnrankedIn<typeof AUTO_APPROVAL_BLOCK_PRECEDENCE>>` asserts that every member MAPPED to a non-null category is RANKED in the precedence array — it says nothing about a missing MAP entry. The guard that makes a missing map entry a compile error is the `satisfies Record<AutoApprovalBlockReason, RefusalCategory | null>` clause at vocabulary.ts:487. The branch's own test comment at persist.test.ts:1216 states it CORRECTLY ("makes the mapped-but-unranked case a `pnpm typecheck` failure"), so the docblock and the suite disagree inside one diff. The conclusion ("you need a value that escaped the union") survives; the citation does not.

findings.title: The held_draft non-goal is structurally sound; the auto_post_revoked / ask_withheld / outreach_withheld / batch_halted non-goal leaves the same fault class open in a different shape, unrecorded
findings.reason: Search performed: `rg "isRefusalLedgerEnabled\(\)"` and `rg "noteRefusalLedgerDark"` over the repo excluding node_modules, docs and *.test.ts; plus every consumer of a POLICY_GATE-style category map. Scope: all seven lanes in REFUSAL_SOURCES. Exclusions: docs and tests. Result: guard 4 in persist.ts is the ONLY early kill-switch read outside write.ts, and resolvePolicyGateRefusal (vocabulary.ts:726) is the ONLY throwing resolver. So the exact #1105 shape has no sibling. held_draft: fully defensible — HELD_DRAFT_REFUSAL_CATEGORY (vocabulary.ts:244, used at persist.ts:1126) is a frozen literal with no map, so a vocabulary hole is impossible there. The five map-indexing lanes are different: auto-policy-downgrade.ts:218 writes `refusalCategory: AUTO_POST_REVOKED_REFUSAL_CATEGORIES[reason]`, so an escapee yields `undefined` rather than a throw, the flag check happens INSIDE writeRefusalEvent, and with the ledger off the lane emits the ledger-dark WARNING — claiming a gap for a row migration 116's NOT NULL would have rejected — while naming no code. Same fault class (an escapee behind a dark ledger is unnamed), different mechanism, and equally compile-guarded by `satisfies`. Deferring is a defensible call; what is missing is that neither the arch-review-log row nor the directory.md row records that the class stays open in five other lanes, so the next reader of "#1105 fixed the unsignalled fault class" will over-read it.

findings.title: [R1-7] (both transports throw) may be redundant with case 4 — no natural single-line mutant isolates it
findings.reason: M-w14 (Sentry `try`/`catch` removed) is the defect class [R1-7] names, and case 12 kills it. But case 4 (`a synchronously throwing Sentry buys a cooldown...`) also makes captureMessage throw synchronously and calls the helper OUTSIDE any `not.toThrow()` wrapper, so on inspection it would fail on the same mutant. I did not measure that pairing — case 4's 2-mutation-per-test budget was already spent on M-w02 and M-w04 — so this is an inspection claim, not a measurement. A mutant that ONLY case 12 kills would have to re-throw conditionally on the logger having failed, which is not a shape any plausible edit produces. Recorded so the case is not deleted on the strength of this note alone; defence-in-depth against a combined-failure escape is a reasonable thing to keep.
